data.narrative:
Magdrive, a seed-stage space and aerospace company founded by Mark Stokes and Thomas Clayson, has raised $22.5M to date. The valuation universe comprises 5 public peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private comparable companies including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and Planet Labs, though none provide sufficiently narrow peer data at the same stage or valuation tier.

Of the three triangulation methods tested, only stage-progression proved applicable. This method anchors to the $22.5M total raised as a proxy for current valuation and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for seed-to-next-stage progression, yielding $56M. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied because target revenue is not on file; the Space & Aerospace sector median P/S of 27.4x across the 6 public comparables exists but lacks a denominator for Magdrive. Peer-median analysis was inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage datapoints within the narrow peer set—the broader 14-company Space & Aerospace peer pool would introduce unacceptable heterogeneity.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $48M to $65M, centered on $56M. This range reflects a 15% sensitivity band around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue disclosure (precluding revenue multiples), limited transaction comps at seed stage in space tech, and the wide variance in technology maturity and capital requirements across the broader peer universe.
